label: rem:chain-spring-modes
title: Spring-like modes of open Hopf chains
html:
Remark. Spring-like modes of open Hopf chains

An open molecular Hopf chain behaves like a topological spring. Free endpoints undergo Reidemeister I moves, and Reidemeister II moves propagate without affecting interior bonds.

Longitudinal modes. A compression or extension corresponds to a correlated sequence of Reidemeister II moves along the backbone.

Bending modes. The chain bends at any interior atom. The bending stiffness depends on the bond order k: single-bond backbones are flexible, double-bond backbones are rigid.

Endpoint oscillation. Free endpoints are soft. Dangling trefoils oscillate at low energies. This is the topological analogue of the stretching vibration of terminal groups.

In a closed ring, these soft modes are quenched. Every atom is interior, and deformation requires a global braid rearrangement.
